name: Benaiah
overview: Benaiah was a male Levite who held the important roles of second rank Levite, gatekeeper, and trumpeter. His service as a gatekeeper and musician highlights his dedicated participation in the worship and temple duties of Israel. There are no additional notes recorded about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Benaiah means 'YHWH has built,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning connected to God's providence. This proper name is noted in 1 Chronicles 15:18 and emphasizes God's active role in the life of this Levite.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Benaiah as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the tribe entrusted with priestly and temple responsibilities. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no further family relationships are recorded.
scriptureSignificance: Benaiah's significance lies in his service as a Levite who contributed to the orderly worship in Israel by serving as a gatekeeper and a trumpeter. These roles were vital for maintaining the sanctity and function of the temple worship under God's covenant people. His mention in 1 Chronicles 15:18 situates him within the broader narrative of temple organization and worship during the time of King David.
